beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Private moderation cannot by itself solve a competition that punishes the moderate participant.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Rules and coordination must make restraint possible without handing unlimited power to gatekeepers.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book also insists that those with greater power carry greater obligations.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its proposal deserves examination precisely where protection, freedom and unequal needs come into tension.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book moves through mythic images, biological cooperation, forbidden lines and technological futures.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The myths make the pattern memorable, while later chapters test the analogy's usefulness.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The endnote states the central claim as a systems hypothesis, not a diagnosis.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That structure lets you examine both the emotional image and its explanatory limits.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You can disagree with a comparison without losing the question it helps formulate.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The detailed chapters supply qualifications that a striking title cannot carry alone.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Readers gain a vocabulary for judging expansion without treating every improvement as suspect.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Begin with A Monster Is a Model to understand the book's interpretive contract.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Then read The Winter Cannibal alongside The Wisdom of Brakes.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Ask how an individual temptation becomes a competitive rule that resists correction.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Keep testing whether a boundary protects people or merely protects its own authority.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book gives that question more room than a simple warning against excess.
